sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Mandacaru is a tree-like cactus of central and eastern Brazil, especially the dry Caatinga landscapes. It usually reaches 3–7 m, with upright, branched, ribbed stems bearing spines. Its large white flowers open at night; the floral tube is about 25–30 cm long.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: The red berry, about 5–8 cm long, contains sweet white pulp eaten fresh or processed. The plate accurately shows the ribbed habit, large night-blooming flower, red fruit and white pulp with black seeds.
